blocks.text: City of Langley Townhomes for Sale

parts.t: These are townhomes for sale in the City of Langley, the compact city surrounded by the Township. Many complexes are a short walk from City Park, Douglas Park or downtown, and two SkyTrain stations are planned on the City’s west side. For every home type in the area, see my
City of Langley homes for sale
page.
Written by
Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®

For townhome buyers in City of Langley and the rest of Langley, I read the strata plan, bylaws and repair records with you before you firm up. I've been a REALTOR® since 2015 and I'm in the top 1% of Fraser Valley REALTORS®. I've also closed more than $500M in sales.

In Paragon, the MLS® system used by local REALTORS®, City of Langley is Langley sub-area F6A. The sections below cover a small city with townhome pockets, SkyTrain stations and parks close to home, plus the checks I run before you write an offer.

blocks.text: A small city with townhome pockets

parts.t: The City of Langley is its own municipality, separate from the Township of Langley that surrounds it. Townhome complexes are spread through its residential neighbourhoods. The City's Official Community Plan sets out where ground-oriented housing is planned.

The Province's Surrey Langley SkyTrain project extends the Expo Line along Fraser Highway into Langley. Langley City Centre Station will sit east of 203 Street and Industrial Avenue with a transit exchange, and Willowbrook Station is at the City's western edge. For townhome owners, that could mean a car-light commute later on.

City Park on 207 Street between 48 and 51 Avenue has ball diamonds, playgrounds, a spray park, trails and an off-leash area. Douglas Park is near downtown, and Timms Community Centre at 20399 Douglas Crescent has a gym, track and weight room.
Form B. The Form B lists fees, levies and insurance.

The City is in the Langley School District. Use the SD35 locator to confirm catchments.

City of Langley townhomes suit buyers who want a garage and some outdoor space, but also want to walk to shops, parks and the community centre. First-time buyers who've outgrown a condo often look here, and so do buyers planning for SkyTrain. If you work in Surrey or farther west, being close to the future stations could make a real difference to your commute. The City has a mix of older and newer complexes, so the age of the building matters as much as the unit.

I go through the strata package with you, check for planned levies and flag anything in the minutes that affects the complex. I'll also compare units across complexes so you can see what you're getting for the fee. Call or text me to book showings for any townhome here.

The City and the Township are separate municipalities, with their own property taxes, bylaws and services. When you compare a City townhome with one in the Township, check the taxes, garbage and recycling service and parking rules for each address.

Before SkyTrain arrives, Langley Centre is the bus hub. The 501 and 502 run to Surrey Central Station, the 503 express runs along Fraser Highway, and the 595 connects to Carvolth Exchange and Maple Meadows Station. The 531 runs between Willowbrook and White Rock Centre.

A townhouse can be a conventional strata or part of a bare land strata. Patios and yards are often limited common property. The contingency reserve fund rules require a yearly top-up of at least 10% of the operating budget.

Elementary schools in the City include Blacklock Fine Arts at 5100 206 Street, Douglas Park Community School at 5409 206 Street, Nicomekl at 20050 53 Avenue and Uplands Elementary & Montessori at 4471 207A Street. H.D. Stafford Middle is at 20441 Grade Crescent. Confirm catchments on the SD35 maps.

1. Where will SkyTrain stop in the City of Langley?
Langley City Centre Station, east of 203 Street and Industrial Avenue. Willowbrook Station is at the City's western edge.
2. Is the City of Langley the same as the Township?
No. The City of Langley is its own municipality, separate from the Township.
3. What parks are near City of Langley townhomes?
City Park on 207 Street, Douglas Park, and Timms Community Centre on Douglas Crescent.
4. Are there flood concerns?
Some areas near the Nicomekl River have flood considerations. Check with the City for the address.
5. Are property taxes different in the City and the Township?
Yes. They are separate municipalities with their own taxes, bylaws and services.
6. Which buses leave from Langley Centre?
Routes 501 and 502 to Surrey Central, the 503 express along Fraser Highway, and the 595 to Carvolth Exchange and Maple Meadows Station, among others.
7. Which elementary schools are in the City of Langley?
Blacklock Fine Arts, Douglas Park Community School, Nicomekl and Uplands Elementary & Montessori. Check catchments with SD35.
